input:
The returns flow costs $261k a year in transport overall. This figure is built up from carrier invoices for the last 12 months: 275 km per trip at $1.53 per km, over 621 trips per year. It is important to note that empty running is included in the trip count, and the cost per trip is the invoiced cost of the whole movement, loaded and empty together; a review that priced only the loaded leg would understate the flow's cost by the empty return it also pays for, giving a misleading picture.
The evidence base is the invoice record rather than a tariff estimate: each trip in the count was actually run and invoiced, and the rate is the average the invoices give. The figure is therefore a record of what the flow cost over the period, at the volumes the period carried. A change in return volume changes the trip count and the cost with it, while the rate per km moves only when the carrier terms change; the two drivers are essentially separate, and the review holds them separate so that a cost movement can be assigned to volume or to rate. The $261k stands as the annual cost of the returns flow on the invoiced basis, for comparison against any change that alters the trip count, the distance, or the rate.
